'''Uri Alon''' ({{Langx|he|אורי אלון}}; born 1969) is an Israeli [[systems biologist]] and professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/mcb/UriAlon/|title=Homepage - Uri Alon|work=weizmann.ac.il}}</ref> His highly cited<ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|fMQZybAAAAAJ}}</ref> research investigates [[gene expression]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Alon | first1 = U. | last2 = Barkai | first2 = N. | last3 = Notterman | first3 = D. A. | last4 = Gish | first4 = K. | last5 = Ybarra | first5 = S. | last6 = Mack | first6 = D. | last7 = Levine | first7 = A. J. | title = Broad patterns of gene expression revealed by clustering analysis of tumor and normal colon tissues probed by oligonucleotide arrays | doi = 10.1073/pnas.96.12.6745 | journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | volume = 96 | issue = 12 | pages = 6745–6750 | year = 1999 | pmid =  10359783| pmc = 21986| bibcode = 1999PNAS...96.6745A | doi-access = free }}</ref> [[network motif]]s<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Milo | first1 = R. | last2 = Shen-Orr | first2 = S. | last3 = Itzkovitz | first3 = S. | last4 = Kashtan | first4 = N. | last5 = Chklovskii | first5 = D. | last6 = Alon | first6 = U. | title = Network Motifs: Simple Building Blocks of Complex Networks | doi = 10.1126/science.298.5594.824 | journal = Science | volume = 298 | issue = 5594 | pages = 824–827 | year = 2002 | pmid =  12399590| bibcode = 2002Sci...298..824M | s2cid = 9884096 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Shen-Orr | first1 = S. S. | last2 = Milo | first2 = R. | last3 = Mangan | first3 = S. | last4 = Alon | first4 = U. | title = Network motifs in the transcriptional regulation network of Escherichia coli | journal = Nature Genetics | volume = 31 | issue = 1 | pages = 64–68 | year = 2002 | pmid = 11967538 | doi = 10.1038/ng881| s2cid = 2180121 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and the design principles of biological networks<ref>{{cite book |author=Uri Alon |title=An introduction to systems biology: design principles of biological circuits |publisher=Chapman & Hall/CRC |location=Boca Raton |year=2007 |isbn=978-1-58488-642-6 }}</ref> in ''[[Escherichia coli]]'' and other organisms using both [[computational biology]] and traditional experimental [[wet laboratory]] techniques.{{cn|date=April 2026}}

==Education==
Alon earned his bachelor's and master's degrees from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] and his [[Ph.D.]] degree in [[Theoretical Physics|theoretical physics]] from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref name="mukamel"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://arxiv.org/find/cond-mat/1/au:+Alon_U/0/1/0/all/0/1|title=arXiv.org Search|work=arxiv.org}}</ref>

==Career==
After having his interest in biology sparked, Alon headed to [[Princeton University]] for his [[postdoctoral]] work in experimental biology.  He returned to the Weizmann Institute as a professor.

Alon features in several popular videos on YouTube such as ''Sunday at the Lab'' (with [[Michael Elowitz]])<ref>{{YouTube|id=yhncg6GXYq8|title="Uri Alon's Song - Sunday at the Lab co-written with Elowitz"}}</ref> and ''How to Give a Good Talk''.<ref>{{YouTube|id=5OFAhBw0OXs|title="How to Give a Good Talk by Uri Alon"}}</ref> As of 2011, he is the author of the most highly bookmarked scientific paper on [[CiteULike]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.citeulike.org/citegeist?days=all |title=CiteULike CiteGeist: Popular Papers |access-date=2011-06-09 |archive-date=2019-03-30 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330032521/http://www.citeulike.org/citegeist?days=all }}</ref> ''How To Choose a Good Scientific Problem''<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Alon | first1 = U. | title = How to Choose a Good Scientific Problem | doi = 10.1016/j.molcel.2009.09.013 | journal = Molecular Cell | volume = 35 | issue = 6 | pages = 726–728 | year = 2009 | pmid =  19782018| url = http://www.weizmann.ac.il/mcb/UriAlon/sites/mcb.UriAlon/files/uploads/nurturing/howtochoosegoodproblem.pdf|access-date=2020-09-16| doi-access = free }}</ref> and ''How to Build a Motivated Research Group''.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Alon | first1 = U. | title = How to Build a Motivated Research Group | doi = 10.1016/j.molcel.2010.01.011 | journal = Molecular Cell | url = http://www.weizmann.ac.il/mcb/UriAlon/sites/mcb.UriAlon/files/uploads/nurturing/howtobuildmotivatedresearchgroup.pdf| volume = 37 | issue = 2 | pages = 151–152 | year = 2010 | pmid =  20122395|access-date=2020-09-16| doi-access = free }}</ref>

In 2021 he was appointed visiting professor in the bioengineering department of [[Stanford University]]. He is a member of the IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Uri Alon |url=https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/speaker/uri-alon/ |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=Biomedical Mathematics Group |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Alon has contributed to the understanding of [[gene regulatory network]]s and generalized the term [[network motif]] in 2002.<ref>R. Milo, S. Shen-Orr, S. Itzkovitz, N. Kashtan, D. Chklovskii, U. Alon: ''Network motifs: simple building blocks of complex networks'', Science 298, 2002, S. 824–827</ref><ref>S. Shen-Orr, R. Milo, S. Mangan, U. Alon: ''Network motifs in the transcriptional regulation network of Escherichia coli'', Nature Genetics 31, 2002,: 64–68</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alon |first1=Uri |title=Network motifs: theory and experimental approaches |journal=Nature Reviews Genetics |date=June 2007 |volume=8 |issue=6 |pages=450–461 |doi=10.1038/nrg2102|pmid=17510665 |s2cid=7169406 }}</ref>

Together with his team, he reunited different theories of [[Endocrine system|endocrine]] [[feedback loop]]s by introducing the closely related concepts of "dynamical compensation" and "autoimmune surveillance of hypersecreting mutants".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karin |first1=O |last2=Swisa |first2=A |last3=Glaser |first3=B |last4=Dor |first4=Y |last5=Alon |first5=U |title=Dynamical compensation in physiological circuits. |journal=Molecular Systems Biology |date=8 November 2016 |volume=12 |issue=11 |page=886 |doi=10.15252/msb.20167216 |pmid=27875241|pmc=5147051 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Maimon |first1=L |last2=Milo |first2=T |last3=Moyal |first3=RS |last4=Mayo |first4=A |last5=Danon |first5=T |last6=Bren |first6=A |last7=Alon |first7=U |title=Timescales of Human Hair Cortisol Dynamics. |journal=iScience |date=26 August 2020 |volume=23 |issue=9 |article-number=101501 |doi=10.1016/j.isci.2020.101501 |pmid=32911331|pmc=7490542 |bibcode=2020iSci...23j1501M }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Korem Kohanim |first1=Y |last2=Tendler |first2=A |last3=Mayo |first3=A |last4=Friedman |first4=N |last5=Alon |first5=U |title=Endocrine Autoimmune Disease as a Fragility of Immune Surveillance against Hypersecreting Mutants. |journal=Immunity |date=19 May 2020 |volume=52 |issue=5 |pages=872–884.e5 |doi=10.1016/j.immuni.2020.04.022 |pmid=32433950|pmc=7237888 }}</ref> The theories are able to explain a plethora of phenomena ranging from [[Circannual cycle|circannual]] endocrine rhythms<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tendler |first1=A |last2=Bar |first2=A |last3=Mendelsohn-Cohen |first3=N |last4=Karin |first4=O |last5=Korem Kohanim |first5=Y |last6=Maimon |first6=L |last7=Milo |first7=T |last8=Raz |first8=M |last9=Mayo |first9=A ==Awards==
In 2004 Alon was awarded the [[Overton Prize]]<ref name="overton"/> for "outstanding accomplishment by a scientist in the early to mid stage of his or her career" by the [[International Society for Computational Biology]]. Alon has also been awarded:
* Moore Fellowship, [[California Institute of Technology]] (2000)
* EMBO Young Investigator Award (2001)
* [[IBM]] Faculty Award (2003)
* Minerva Junior Research Group on Biological Computation (2003)
* Morris L. Levinson Award in Biology (2003)
* Teva Founders Prize (2005)
* [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] membership (2007)<ref name="F1000">{{cite web|url=http://f1000.com/thefaculty/member/4073092881186037|title=Uri Alon|work=f1000.com|access-date=2011-06-09|archive-date=2012-03-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323161543/http://f1000.com/thefaculty/member/4073092881186037}}</ref>
* [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]] fellow 2009<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.radcliffe.edu/fellowships/fellows_2010ualon.aspx |title=Radcliffe Fellows |access-date=2011-06-09 |archive-date=2011-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606164831/http://www.radcliffe.edu/fellowships/fellows_2010ualon.aspx }}</ref>
* [[Human Frontier Science Program#HFSP Nakasone Award|HFSP Nakasone Award]] (2014)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hfsp.org/awardees/hfsp-nakasone-award/2014-award|title=2014 HFSP Nakasone Award goes to Uri Alon|work=hfsp.org|access-date=2014-06-12|archive-date=2019-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425210839/http://www.hfsp.org/awardees/hfsp-nakasone-award/2014-award}}</ref>
